qualifications: Repeated related genomes do not establish independent observations. OarX/FmnO blank assignments do not demonstrate absence; organism inclusion and homolog detection bias can produce association. None of these retained cases defines a universal association significance threshold.

evidence.observation: The target genome has dispersed chorismate genes. In Aeropyrum pernix and Pyrococcus abyssi, an unknown GHMP-kinase-like gene lies immediately downstream of shikimate dehydrogenase. Its homologs occur in pathway-bearing archaea but not the pathway-lacking P. horikoshii comparison. A separate GHMP paralog, RMJ01903, tracks threonine-biosynthesis genes in other archaeal genomes.
evidence.limit: Complete main paper, genome-analysis methods, results, and substrate-assay methods read. No WIT reconstruction, alignment, or enzyme assay rerun. Historical WIT identifier retained without an unverified modern-locus mapping. | Group source-use limits: Related genome occurrences are not asserted independent tests. The historical WIT/gi identity is preserved without an invented modern locus mapping; none of the analyses was rerun.

evidence.observation: The authors’ preceding genomic search associated QueCDEF with queuosine. QueF lacks an archaeal counterpart, unlike QueCDE. Cyclohydrolase assays were negative with positive controls. Reconsidering the distribution placed QueF after preQ0, the shared queuosine/archaeosine intermediate. Lack of a B12-binding motif favored testing preQ0 reduction before epoxyqueuosine reduction.
